If you're planning a wedding, you obviously want it to run smoothly, to be full of blessing, and to line up with your faith. In Islam, a marriage isn't simply two people joining — it's an act of worship, and a deeply sacred one. Which makes it genuinely important to know how an Islamic marriage is meant to be done.

So here's the full breakdown, so your big day isn't only romantic but blessed with it.

💍 What Marriage Means in Islam

Marriage in Islam isn't only about love. It's a form of obedience to Allah SWT and to the Sunnah of the Prophet SAW. Its purpose goes beyond joining two people:

  1. Carrying out the command of Allah and the Sunnah of the Prophet
  2. Guarding yourself against zina
  3. Building a household that is sakinah, mawaddah, wa rahmah

With the right intention and a process that follows sharia, a marriage becomes a source of reward and a doorway to paradise.

✨ How a Marriage Works in Islam

Below are the stages of an Islamic marriage you need to know. All of them are laid out in the Qur'an and in authentic hadith, so this isn't just religiously valid — insya Allah it's full of blessing too.

1. Khitbah (The Proposal)

The first step on the way to the aisle is the khitbah, the formal proposal to your intended. In Islam, the man usually comes to propose to the woman with the clear intention of marrying her.

🔹 One important note: Islam firmly forbids proposing to a woman who is already spoken for, unless the earlier proposal has been withdrawn or turned down. That etiquette exists to protect everyone's dignity and feelings.

2. Akad Nikah – The Core of an Islamic Wedding

Once the proposal is accepted and both families agree, you reach the most sacred stage of all: the akad nikah, the Islamic marriage contract.

Before the ijab qabul, there's usually a khutbah nikah (khutbatun nikah) delivered by the officiant or an ustaz. It's a marriage sermon carrying prayers and guidance for an Islamic household.

An akad nikah has to meet 5 core conditions:

  1. Both parties present
  2. Ijab and qabul (the offer of marriage and its acceptance)
  3. Mahar (the bridal gift)
  4. A wali nikah, the guardian (usually the bride's father)
  5. Two male witnesses of good standing

If all of those are satisfied and the ijab qabul is done properly, the marriage is valid under sharia.

3. Walimah – The Wedding Feast the Sunnah Recommends

After the akad it's time for the walimatul ‘ursy, the wedding reception. In Islam the walimah is sunnah muakkadah — strongly encouraged — and it can even become obligatory where announcing the marriage to the community matters.

But remember, a walimah doesn't have to be lavish. The Prophet SAW himself once held a simple walimah serving nothing but dates and milk.

💡 Tips from the Sunnah:

  1. Make a point of inviting people in need
  2. Don't go overboard, and don't let anything sinful creep in
  3. Treat the walimah as an act of gratitude and a chance to share

🎯 The Higher Purpose of Marriage in Islam

Marriage exists for more than emotional and physical needs. Islam sees it as a path toward:

  1. Guarding your own purity
  2. Completing half of your faith
  3. Raising a righteous generation
  4. Making a family life that is harmonious and full of affection

The Bottom Line: Marriage Is Worship, Not Just Tradition

Marrying in Islam isn't only about being valid in the eyes of the law or of society — it's about being valid before Allah SWT. Which is exactly why it matters so much to follow the process the sharia lays out.

From a sincere intention, to a khitbah done well, to a valid akad nikah, to a walimah full of blessing — all of it is worship. And like any act of worship, the more sincere it is and the closer it follows the guidance, the greater the reward and the pleasure Allah grants you.

About Park Hyatt

On the hunt for a Jakarta wedding venue that is elegant, easy to get to, and flexible enough to bend around your concept? Park Hyatt Jakarta belongs on your wishlist, no question!

This five-star hotel has the whole package: a prestigious Menteng address, lavishly designed rooms, modern facilities, and of course a view over Jakarta that turns the drama up a notch on your ceremony.

Room Types

1. Park Room (57 m²)

  1. Starting on the 25th floor - elevated city views
  2. One King or Two Twin beds - flexible arrangements
  3. Spacious work desk - modern business amenities
  4. Contemporary furnishings - Indonesian touches on an international design

2. Park Suite Deluxe (85 m²)

  1. More space, with uninterrupted Jakarta views
  2. Separate areas - distinct living & sleeping zones

  2. King bed in a separate bedroom

The Residences

Capacity: 500 guests (standing), 252 guests (25 round tables)

Description: An indoor space that feels like a very expensive home. Open kitchen, private bar — right for an intimate wedding with a warm, exclusive mood.

Capacity: Up to 1,400 guests

Description: The newest room, half indoors and half out. A modern garden wedding concept — lavish, and open to the sky.

The Observatory

Capacity: 200 guests (standing)

Description: The highest venue in the building! A full 360-degree panorama of Jakarta. Ideal for an exclusive wedding that stays intimate and seriously classy.

Restaurants at Park Hyatt

1. KITA Restaurant

KITA 喜多 serves the real flavours of modern Japanese cooking — Teppanyaki, Shabu-Shabu, Tempura, Robatayaki, Sushi, Sashimi — all of it coming out of a lively open kitchen. There are nine private rooms, each one with a stunning view over the city.

2. Kita Bar

One of the highest rooftop bars in Jakarta, KITA Bar is a stylish spot running on cheer, energy and straightforward fun.

It offers a drinking experience with a difference: a range of craft cocktails paired with games and entertainment, plus Izakaya-style small plates.

3. The Bar

At The Bar on the 23rd floor, we invite you into an oasis of charm and grace where classic sophistication meets the restless energy of the city. Enjoy meticulously built cocktails, live jazz and fine cigars, all against a backdrop of breathtaking panoramic views. Discover the rich heritage behind our signature drinks as their secrets give themselves up sip by sip. Sink into a room where every last detail reflects timeless refinement and a quiet, hidden allure.

Up on the 22nd floor, the Dining Room lays out a genuinely tempting buffet of authentic Indonesian dishes from Java alongside regional Italian cooking built on the best local produce. The bright, stylish interior comes with an open kitchen, so guests can talk to our chefs while they work. Four semi-private rooms are ideal for business meetings, family occasions and intimate events.

The Conservatory on the lobby floor has four distinct areas, each with its own character and its own stunning view of the city's landmarks. Meeting friends, getting work done, or simply reading — there is a setting here to match whatever mood you walked in with, and to make the whole thing that bit more comfortable.

About Kempinski

Hotel Indonesia Kempinski Jakarta isn't just another hotel, bestie! It's a piece of history — standing since 1962, quietly watching Jakarta grow up around it. After a top-to-bottom renovation in 2009 it came back with the luxury dialled all the way up, under Kempinski Hotels, the oldest hotel group in Europe and one with a reputation nobody's about to question.

Sitting right on the iconic Bundaran HI, its location is so central that this venue has become the first choice for couples chasing a wedding nobody forgets. Just picture it — getting married in a building that counts as genuine national pride!

Room Types

  1. Deluxe Room - Perfect for guests coming in from out of town, with a cosy courtyard view
  2. Grand Deluxe Room - Sleeps 3, with a spectacular view over the Jakarta skyline
  3. Grand Deluxe Executive Room - A step up in luxury, with afternoon tea service + access to the Ganesha Executive Club Lounge
  4. Presidential Suite - The ultimate flex! 412 m² with a private spa, a separate living room, a dining room and a whirlpool that has you feeling like royalty

Amenities

  2. Flat-screen TV with satellite channels
  3. Coffee/tea makers in every room

  7. 24-hour concierge service, ready for whatever you need

  2. Fitness Center

Kempinski Grand Ballroom

Here's the main character, the wedding venue that stops every guest in their tracks. Up on the 11th floor of Grand Indonesia West Mall, this ballroom is literally breathtaking:

  1. Capacity: Up to 3,500 guests for a cocktail reception, or 1,000 guests for a seated dinner
  2. Size: A hugely generous 2,700 m²
  3. Highlight: An opulent black Swarovski chandelier — the statement piece the whole room is built around
  4. Access: A private lobby drop-off, separate from the mall entrance + dedicated parking for VIP guests

Perfect for the couple who want a grand wedding with the luxury dial pushed clean off the charts!

Bali Room

If you'd rather keep it intimate, with a guest list up to 1,000, the Bali Room is the hidden gem you're after:

  1. Ambiance: Rich in heritage, with Indonesian cultural touches
  2. Capacity: Ideal for 800-1,000 guests
  3. Special Feature: It can be transformed into a full fairy-tale setting

Ramayana Terrace

If you're after outdoor vibes and natural light, this is your spot!

  1. Concept: A multifunction tropical garden in the middle of the city
  2. Location: A heritage building dating back to the 1960s (where President Soekarno held state dinners!)
  3. Feature: A 135 m² glass-doomed dome whose natural light turns a beautiful blue in the late afternoon
  4. Unique: Amphitheatre-style steps, perfect for creative wedding setups

Heritage Room

Up on the 16th floor, with a stunning city skyline view:

  1. Concept: Perfect for a traditional akad nikah ceremony — the Islamic marriage contract itself
  2. Feature: 2 function rooms with a dedicated kitchen
  3. View: Breathtaking city views from up high
  4. Vibe: Intimate and sacred, for a once-in-a-lifetime moment

The Meeting Room Collection

The hotel has 13 meeting rooms and 6 boardrooms that can be adapted for all sorts of wedding prep, such as

  1. The wedding blessing
  2. Teapay
  3. Makeup room

1. Signatures Restaurant - The Heritage Taste 🇮🇩

A must-try for a reception dinner with an Indonesian touch:

  1. Specialty: The legendary Bubur Ayam HI, the signature dish here
  2. Concept: Indonesian & international cuisine with real heritage vibes
  3. Ambiance: Art & photography celebrating Hotel Indonesia's history
  4. Special: Sunday brunch with Alaskan King Crab, lobster and prime rib

2. OKU - Japanese Sophistication 🍣

For the Japanese-food lovers and the zen-vibes crowd:

  1. Concept: A premium Japanese restaurant with a sophisticated ambiance
  2. Specialty: The Okukase tasting menu (6 courses) with Japanese A5 Miyazaki Wagyu beef
  3. Signature Dishes: OKU Karaage, Salmon Aburi, Soft Shell Crab Roll
  4. Vibe: A cool, jazzy atmosphere, perfect for the modern couple

3. Paulaner Bräuhaus - German Authenticity 🍺

Indonesia's only microbrewery restaurant — you genuinely won't find this anywhere else!

  1. Capacity: 200 seats with a spectacular city view
  2. Specialty: Traditional Bavarian cooking + authentic German beer
  3. Entertainment: Live music performances + the big sporting events on large screens
  4. Special Event: The annual Oktoberfest, bringing the German spirit to Indonesia
  5. Signature: Crispy Pork Knuckle, Bavarian Sausage Platter, Fresh Lager Beer

4. Kempi Deli - Grab & Go Delights 🥐

Perfect for wedding-prep snacks:

  1. Concept: A fine-food delicatessen with home-made products
  2. Specialty: 30 types of authentic European bread and pastry
  3. Products: Sausages, cold cuts and artisanal treats

5. Sky Pool Bar & Café - Rooftop Goals! 🌆

An Instagram-worthy spot with the Jakarta skyline behind you:

  1. Vibes: A rooftop bar with a swimming pool
  2. Drinks: Spectacular cocktails, Long Island iced tea, mojito, tequila sunrise
  3. Perfect for: Pre-wedding photo sessions, or the bachelor/bachelorette party

If you've been reading up on Chinese wedding traditions, you're in exactly the right place! A Chinese wedding isn't only full of colour — every part of it carries meaning, and there are luck symbols everywhere you look. Plenty of Chinese-Indonesian couples go modern with the day now, but the customs stay a core part of this sacred moment.

So in this article we're working through the lot: the stages of a traditional Chinese wedding, the symbols that matter, and the myths people still genuinely believe. Let's get into it.

The Stages of a Chinese Wedding: From Pre-Wedding to After the Reception

1. The Chinese-Style Lamaran (Mak Comblang Time!)

In Chinese tradition the lamaran — the formal proposal — works a little differently. Here the groom's family sends an intermediary, the mak comblang or matchmaker, to let the bride's family know their son would make a good match. After that both families go hunting for an auspicious date for the formal proposal.

2. Sangjit: The Gift-Giving Moment That's Genuinely Special

Sangjit is a big deal in the run-up to the day, usually held anywhere from a week to a month before the wedding. This is the day the groom's family arrives at the bride's family home carrying the seserahan, the gifts the groom's side brings over. A Sangjit haul usually holds:

  1. A full outfit, plus jewellery and cosmetics
  2. Party money and angpau, the red envelopes of cash
  3. Sweet fruit, candied treats and foods that stand for good fortune
  4. Red candles
  5. Alcohol, usually arak or wine
  6. 12 tins of food, such as pork trotters or longan

Sangjit is also the moment the two extended families properly meet each other over a meal. Rather lovely, isn't it?

3. Picking an Auspicious Date: Nobody Just Grabs a Weekend

Chinese families take the date extremely seriously — the day, the month, even the hour all have to line up and be lucky. The right date usually comes out of the lunar calendar or a feng shui calculation. The point of it? A marriage that stays harmonious and never runs short.

4. The Send-Off Party, or Liauw Tiaa

Before they're officially husband and wife, the bride and groom mark the end of single life with friends and family. It's usually held at the bride's house, and it runs on games, food and long easy conversations with relatives.

5. The Cia Tao Ceremony: Prayers Before the Big Day

Cia Tao is a sequence of prayers honouring God, the ancestors and your parents. It starts at home, moves on to the temple, then comes back home again for the tribute to your parents. It carries real weight, because it marks the spiritual blessing of both the family and the universe.

The Big Day: The Chinese Wedding Ceremony, Sacred and Loaded With Meaning

1. The Buddhist Blessing

If the couple are Buddhist, the blessing takes place at the vihara, led by a Pandita and the bhikkhunis. It's a long sequence — the procession in, the reading of the vows, the exchange of rings, right through to handing over the marriage certificate. Every step of it carries spiritual weight.

2. Tea Pai: The Tea Ceremony That Gets Everyone Emotional

Tea Pai is the moment the couple serve tea to their parents and to the elders on both sides. In return they get advice, blessings and gifts — jewellery or cash, usually. At heart it's a mark of respect and the family's blessing rolled into one.

After the Reception: More Traditions to Tie the Families Together

1. Cia Kiang Say

Once the party's over, the newlyweds are formally “introduced” to the bride's extended family. This is the husband's official meeting with his wife's relatives. Usually after this the two of them can properly live under one roof.

2. Cia Ceem

Cia Ceem is the mirror image: now it's the wife's turn to be introduced to her husband's extended family. It also signals that she's been accepted as a new member of that family.

The Symbols That Matter in a Chinese Wedding

In a Chinese wedding every element means something. Here are a few key symbols worth knowing:

  1. The Colour Red: happiness, luck and prosperity. No wonder the decor goes all in on it!
  2. The Number Eight (8): counted as a lucky number because it sounds like the word for “prosperous” in Chinese.
  3. Dragon & Phoenix: the harmony between man and woman. The dragon is masculine strength; the phoenix is feminine grace.
  4. Food: long noodles = a long life, steamed cupcakes = fertility, and plenty more besides!

Chinese Wedding Myths People Still Believe

Modern as everything has got, the myths around Chinese weddings are alive and well. Here's a look at a few of them:

  1. Don't put the wedding dress on before the day. It brings bad luck, so the story goes!
  2. Don't be a bridesmaid or groomsman more than three times. Break that one, apparently, and you'll struggle to marry at all.
  3. Avoid a partner 3, 5 or 9 years apart in age. Said to be unlucky. Four years apart, though? That one's a good sign!
  4. Eat cake from the couple? You might find your own match sooner!
  5. Anyone on the committee who doesn't get an angpau could end up unlucky. Which is why the scramble for red envelopes isn't purely for the fun of it!

Wrapping Up: Keeping Tradition Alive in a Modern Age

Chinese wedding traditions are rich in culture and rich in meaning. From Sangjit to Tea Pai, every piece of it carries a spiritual and family message. Times have changed and life has got a lot more modern, but keeping and respecting the traditions is a way of honouring your ancestors and what your family stands for.

If you're in the middle of planning a Chinese wedding, hopefully this helps. Pick a good date, put the seserahan together the way tradition asks, and above all—enjoy the process!

If you or your partner are Buddhist and there's a wedding on the horizon, it really is worth knowing how a Buddhist ceremony is put together. It isn't only sacred and steeped in tradition — it's loaded with meaning and a genuinely deep philosophy of love.

In Buddhist teaching, marriage isn't an obligation. It's a choice. So if you decide to marry, what you're really saying is that you're ready to build a home on loving kindness (metta), compassion (karuna) and empathy (mudita).

The Buddhist Philosophy of Marriage

In Buddhist teaching, marriage is about a strong inner bond between two people. The goal? A family that holds each other up, is full of happiness, and gives you both somewhere to grow — in this life and in the ones still to come.

Buddhist teaching also insists on monogamy. You'll find it set out in Anguttara Nikaya 11.57:

“The marriage praised by the Buddha is the marriage between a good man (deva) and a good woman (devi).”


Where a Buddhist Wedding Can Be Held

A Buddhist wedding can take place in a few different settings:

  1. A vihara, the Buddhist temple
  2. A cetiya, the smaller shrine hall
  3. The home of either the bride or the groom (as long as it meets the requirements)

So you can pick whatever suits you for comfort and for numbers.

The Buddhist Wedding Prep Checklist

Here's the kit you'll need ready to run a Buddhist wedding ceremony:

  1. An altar with a Buddha statue (Buddha Rupang)
  2. Candles in five colours (blue, yellow, red, white, orange)
  3. An incense holder and nine sticks of scented incense
  4. A glass or bowl of water + flowers (for the sprinkling)
  5. Two vases of flowers + two plates of fruit for the offering
  6. Wedding rings 💍
  7. Yellow cloth (90 x 125 cm²) + yellow ribbon (100 cm)
  8. Cushions or seating for the couple, the pandita and the bhikkhu
  9. The marriage vow certificate
  10. A dana offering for the bhikkhu (if one is attending)

The Buddhist Wedding Running Order (Step by Step)

Here's the full rundown of a Buddhist wedding ceremony you can follow:

1. The Pandita Opens

The pandita and their assistant take their places. The couple come in and stand in front of the altar.

2. A Few Quick Questions

The pandita asks whether both of them are going through with this freely, with nobody pushing them into it. If the answer's “yes”, the ceremony carries on!

3. Lighting the Five Coloured Candles

These aren't ordinary candles, mind. Every colour means something:

  1. Blue (lit by the groom's mother): devotion to the Triratna & to the family.
  2. Orange (the groom's father): the drive to build a home together.
  3. Yellow (the bride's mother): wisdom in family life.
  4. White (the bride's father): purity in thought and in action.
  5. Red (by the pandita): universal loving kindness 💖

4. The Flower & Fruit Offering

The couple offer flowers and fruit as a mark of respect.

5. Reciting the Namaskara Gatha

The central prayer of a Buddhist ceremony, said together with the whole congregation:

ARAHAM SAMMA SAMBUDDHO BHAGAVA

BUDDHAM BHAGAVANTAM ABHIVADEMI

SVAKKHATO BHAGAVATA DHAMMO

DHAMMAM NAMASSAMI

SUPATIPANNO BHAGAVATO SAVAKASANGHO

SANGHAM NAMAMI

6. Reciting the Vandana (3x)

The prayer of homage to the Buddha:

NAMO TASSA BHAGAVATO ARAHATO

SAMMA SAMBUDDHASSA

7. The Marriage Vows

The couple read out their vows, then place the rings on each other's fingers. 💍

8. The Ribbon & the Yellow Cloth

Both of them wear the yellow cloth, tied with the yellow ribbon as a symbol of two souls joined. After that, their

parents and the pandita sprinkle the blessed water.

9. The Symbolic Close

The ribbon and the yellow cloth come off, and then:

  1. Marriage advice from the pandita
  2. Signing the Marriage Vow Certificate
  3. A closing Namaskara led by the pandita

If you liked this one, send it to your partner or your family so everyone turns up ready, inside and out! 🙌

If you and your partner are Buddhist and a wedding is on the cards, you absolutely need to know how the ceremony works and what makes a marriage valid under Buddhist teaching. Yes, marriage isn't an obligation in Buddhism — but once you're sure, it has to be done with full awareness, with loving kindness, and in line with the Dharma.

So, to spare you the confusion, let's go through a Buddhist wedding properly: the legal basis, the principles it rests on, the paperwork you need, right through to the blessing ceremony itself. Stick with us to the end.

What Is Marriage in Buddhist Teaching?

In Buddhism, marriage isn't a spiritual requirement so much as a life choice. The Buddha never obliged anyone to marry, but he did teach that if you choose to, the relationship should be lived through metta (loving kindness), karuna (compassion), mudita (empathy) and upekkha (equanimity).

The Buddhist view is that marriage exists to build a harmonious family full of love, happy in this life, and creating merit for the lives to come. Sounds deep, right?

The Legal Basis for a Buddhist Marriage in Indonesia

Before we get to the rituals, a quick look at the law. In Indonesia, marriage is governed by Law No. 1 of 1974 on Marriage, which says:

“Marriage is a bond of body and soul between a man and a woman as husband and wife, formed to build a happy and lasting family based on belief in the One Almighty God.”

And here's the crucial bit: a marriage only counts as valid when it's carried out according to the religious law of the couple involved. So for Buddhists, the wedding has to follow Buddhist teaching and then be registered with the state.

The Principles Behind a Buddhist Marriage

Buddhist marriage runs on monogamy. That comes from Anguttara Nikaya 11.57, which describes the ideal marriage as one between a good man (deva) and a good woman (devi). So no, there's no version of this where you have more than one partner at a time.

Buddhist teaching also puts four principles at the centre of married life:

  1. Samma Saddha – right faith in the Buddha's teaching, and a commitment to building a family on the Dharma.
  2. Samma Sila – good ethics and morals as the foundation of a harmonious life.
  3. Samma Cagga – generosity, meaning a willingness to give and to understand each other.
  4. Samma Panna – wisdom, so problems get solved without ego getting in the way.

These four really matter — they're the foundation your marriage gets built on!

The Paperwork for a Buddhist Wedding

Beyond the spiritual side, there's admin to sort before the day. Getting it right keeps both the blessing and the civil registration running smoothly.

Here's what the vihara and the civil registry office usually ask for:

  1. The blessing form from the vihara
  2. Photocopies of the KTP — the national ID card — for the couple, their parents and the witnesses, legalised at the kelurahan, your local administrative office
  3. A photocopy of the couple's KK, the family card
  4. Photocopies of the couple's birth certificates
  5. A Surat Keterangan Belum Menikah — the certificate of single status — from the kelurahan
  6. Photocopies of the KTP for the witnesses on each side

On top of that, couples are usually asked to sit through a bimbingan perkawinan session — marriage guidance, essentially pre-wedding counselling — to get themselves ready mentally and spiritually.

How the Buddhist Wedding Blessing Works

Once the paperwork's all in, it's on to the most sacred part — the blessing, the Buddhist wedding ceremony itself. It can be held at a vihara, a cetiya, the home of either the bride or groom, or somewhere else entirely, a hotel for instance (with adjustments — no incense, say, if the venue won't allow it).

Here's how it usually runs:

  1. The couple enter – walked to the Buddha altar by their parents and the witnesses.
  2. Offerings at the altar – the couple offer flowers, fruit, candles and incense as a mark of respect to the Buddha.
  3. Questions – the pandita asks whether they're marrying of their own free will.
  4. Reading the vows – the couple read out their sacred promises and their commitment to each other.
  5. Exchanging rings – the symbol of a bond of body and soul.
  6. The yellow ribbon and cloth – the sign that the marriage is valid and spiritually blessed.
  7. The blessing – the pandita and the parents sprinkle holy water as a symbol of purification.
  8. Dharma advice – the pandita gives a talk on married life within the Dharma.
  9. Removing the ribbon and cloth – marking the start of a new life.
  10. Signing the vow certificate – witnessed by the parents and the official witnesses.
  11. Closing – words of thanks and a prayer said together.

The whole thing runs quiet and full of meaning. No party music, no lavish decor — and that's exactly what makes a Buddhist ceremony beautiful. The focus stays on the spiritual meaning and on being fully present.

A Few Extra Tips If You're Getting Married the Buddhist Way

Talk to the vihara: every council and every vihara can have slightly different technical details, so have that conversation early.

Check with the venue: if you want to marry outside a vihara (a hotel, say), make sure they'll allow the candles and the incense.

Pick an experienced pandita or bhikkhu: it keeps the ceremony smooth and properly solemn.

Keep the documentation simple but sacred: a Buddhist ceremony isn't a loud affair, but intimate coverage still makes it memorable.

In Closing: Marriage in Buddhist Teaching = Awareness & Love Without Conditions

A Buddhist marriage isn't just a ceremony, it's a sacred moment binding two people in universal loving kindness. The process is simple, but it's full of deep values — from honouring the Triratna (Buddha, Dhamma, Sangha) through to a promise to live a good life together.

If you and your partner want to build a home on a strong spiritual foundation, a Buddhist wedding could be the most meaningful choice you make.

Chinese weddings aren’t just famous for all that bold red and gold — they’re also loaded with deep meaning and traditions handed down through generations. From the proposal right through to sharing tea with both sets of parents, every stage carries a philosophy of good wishes: happiness, money flowing in, and a marriage that stays harmonious for life.

If you’re hunting for modern Chinese wedding inspiration — or you just want to understand it properly — here are the 10 stages of Chinese wedding tradition that still hold up and still mean something.

1. Turning Up at Her Parents’ Place to Say You’re Serious

Way back when, the groom-to-be would go and state his intentions in person, turning up at her parents’ house to say he was serious about proposing. And not alone, either: he’d usually bring his immediate family along, everyone in their best clothes.

The big one: be on time! It’s a mark of respect and proof you mean business in front of the bride’s family. Don’t leave your future in-laws waiting.

2. The Lamaran, a.k.a. Guo Da Li

If step one goes down well, next comes Guo Da Li — the lamaran, the formal engagement visit. This is where the groom’s side arrives carrying the sangjit seserahan, the gift trays handed over to the bride’s family. And they don’t mess around. There are usually 10 key items, including:

  1. Red trays: a symbol of happiness and joy. The number of trays brought over has to be even.
  2. Angpau, the red money envelopes (milk money + party money) Milk money is the groom-to-be’s way of repaying the bride’s parents for raising her. Party money is the bridal gift handed to the bride-to-be herself.
  3. One set of women’s clothing. To show that the groom-to-be can provide for his bride
  4. Body care products. The idea being that the bride-to-be keeps looking after herself and looking lovely, especially on the wedding day itself
  5. Gold jewellery. The binding token between the groom-to-be and the bride-to-be. This gift is also a symbol of hope that married life will always be wrapped in good fortune.
  6. Fruit in an even number, as a symbol of peace, happiness, abundant fortune and prosperity.
  7. Red candles with a dragon & phoenix on them. Both have to be red and tied with red ribbon. Why? As a symbol of safety, protection, and warding off any negative energy that shows up as the wedding gets close.
  8. Canned food or pork trotters. Pork trotters are a symbol of safety. If there aren’t any, canned food works instead, and again it has to be an even number.
  9. Sweet & sticky cakes. Symbolising a married life that stays harmonious and showered with fortune.
  10. Two bottles of red wine or champagne. These symbolise good luck, and not only for the couple — for both sets of parents too. Everything brought over gets answered with two bottles of red syrup, which the bride-to-be gives to the groom-to-be.

Later, the bride’s side responds with two bottles of red syrup as a sign of acceptance. Romantic, and still very much traditional!

3. Pick a Lucky Date, Feng Shui Style

For luck and longevity, the wedding date gets chosen from both partners’ zodiac animals and birth elements. That usually means consulting a feng shui expert, or someone who really knows how to read auspicious days. Crucial for the future of the household, apparently!

4. Invitations in Red and Gold

Once the date is locked in, the invitations go to print. They’re usually dominated by red and gold with the “Double Happiness” character (囍), the non-negotiable icon of a Chinese wedding.

Classic design plus a modern touch keeps your invitation current without cutting it off from its roots.

5. Setting Up the Bridal Bed

Two or three days before the wedding, the bride’s family prepares the bedroom for the newlyweds. Sheets, pillows, blanket — all red, obviously.

Don’t forget the fruit in the room, a symbol of fertility. But remember: nobody is allowed to sit on that bed until the big day!

6. The Hair-Combing Ritual (Deeply Philosophical!)

The night before, there’s a hair-combing ceremony loaded with meaning. The bride- or groom-to-be bathes in citrus-infused water, then puts on red clothes and new slippers.

While a happily married woman combs their hair, four blessings are spoken:

  1. First stroke: a union that lasts
  2. Second stroke: harmony forever
  3. Third stroke: many children
  4. Fourth stroke: fortune flowing and a long life

After that, the hair is pinned with red thread and cypress leaves. So meaningful!

7. The Outfit Has to Have Red & Gold

Chinese wedding outfits are usually packed with symbols:

  1. Red = love, luck, happiness
  2. Gold = wealth and abundance
  3. Dragon & phoenix = balance
  4. Mandarin ducks = fidelity
  5. 24K gold pig necklace = fertility

Put it all together and the look is elegant and full of good wishes at the same time.

8. The Fun Part: Collecting the Bride

The pickup is usually loud in the best possible way — gongs, a dragon dance, the whole celebratory racket.

The groom can only get into his bride’s house once the door is opened by the youngest member of her family. Whoever opens it gets an angpau, and answers it with a mandarin orange—a symbol of good luck.

9. The Groom’s Test of Love, a.k.a. Chuangmen

Before he’s allowed anywhere near his bride, the groom has to pass a test first. It’s called Chuangmen — basically a set of “games” from the bridesmaids and the bride’s family, designed to prove the guy is serious.

The challenges might be:

  1. Answering questions about his partner
  2. Eating food in four flavours (bitter, sweet, spicy, sour)
  3. Hunting down the bride’s hidden shoes

Only once he’s through does he get to see his bride and move on to the tea ceremony.

10. Tea Pai: Tea, and Respect for the Parents

This is one of the most moving moments of the lot. Tea Pai is the tea ceremony where the couple show their respect to both sets of parents.

The tea is brewed with sugar, red dates, longan and lotus seeds, then served in "Double Happiness" cups.

The couple will:

  1. Offer tea to the parents while saying: "Please accept and drink this tea."
  2. Then receive angpau & jewellery as a blessing

Only after that is the couple considered properly ready to marry in the eyes of faith and of the state.

Closing: Traditions That Still Fit & Still Mean Something

Times have changed, but Chinese wedding traditions still work in the modern era. Beyond bringing two families closer, every stage carries meaning and good wishes.

So if you want to blend the traditional with the current on your big day, Chinese wedding rituals give you something meaningful and seriously Instagrammable at the same time.

71000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000038.body_en:
Want your first dance with your partner to be unforgettable and full of feeling? Relax, we’ve got you. The first dance at the reception has become one of those traditions that keeps getting bigger among younger couples. Beyond being romantic, it’s the moment that melts the guests too.

But here’s something you might not know: the first dance didn’t originally belong to the couple at all. In 16th-century Europe, it was the guests who danced first, as a way of honouring the newlyweds. Only now does the couple take the floor first, as a symbol of their love and commitment.

The first dance usually happens after dinner, and is followed by dances with the parents. To really land the mood, the song has to be right. So here are 30 romantic songs from across the decades that would make a perfect soundtrack for your first dance.

The 30 Best First Dance Songs of All Time 💃

1. Little Things – One Direction

2. Daylight – Taylor Swift

3. All of Me – John Legend

4. Baby I'm Yours – Arctic Monkeys

5. The Way You Look Tonight – Frank Sinatra

6. It’s Been A Long, Long Time – Harry James

7. Love Me Tender – Elvis Presley

8. Can’t Help Falling in Love – Elvis Presley

9. Stand by Me – Ben E. King

10. Just the Way You Are – Billy Joel

11. Endless Love – Lionel Richie & Diana Ross

12. She – Elvis Costello

13. Make You Feel My Love – Adele

14. The Way You Look Tonight – Tony Bennett

15. I Swear – All-4-One

16. Put Your Head on My Shoulder – Paul Anka

17. La Vie En Rose – Édith Piaf

18. The Power of Love – Celine Dion

19. Can’t Take My Eyes Off You – Frankie Valli

20. We’ve Only Just Begun – The Carpenters

21. Can You Feel The Love Tonight – Boyce Avenue ft. Connie Talbot

22. Embraceable You – Judy Garland

23. My Love Mine All Mine – Mitski

24. Hopelessly Devoted to You – Olivia Newton-John

25. Eternal Flame – The Bangles

26. Will Always Love You – Whitney Houston

27. From This Moment On – Shania Twain ft. Bryan White

28. Can You Feel the Love Tonight – Elton John

29. I Finally Found Someone – Barbra Streisand & Bryan Adams

30. Perfect – Ed Sheeran

How to Pick a First Dance Song That Makes the Moment More Intimate 🎶

  1. Look for something with personal meaning
  2. Pick a song that tells your story as a couple. Maybe the one that was playing when you got together, or the soundtrack from your first film date.
  3. Match the tempo to your taste
  4. Chill, dreamy or fun? It all comes down to tempo. And if you’re not much of a dancer, a slow dance is plenty.
  5. Match it to your wedding theme
  6. Planning an intimate wedding, an outdoor party, an elegant ballroom do? Pick a song that sits inside that atmosphere.

Pro Tips for a Memorable First Dance

  1. Practice together: carve out time to rehearse — it doubles as bonding time!
  2. Choose comfortable shoes: tall heels look great, but going down mid-dance... not cute.
  3. Have a backup plan: keep an alternative playlist ready just in case of technical issues.
  4. Enjoy the moment: don’t stress about being perfect, what matters is that you two are happy!

Ready to create your own fairytale moment? Save this playlist and start practising now! Your wedding first dance will be the sweetest talking point for years to come.

Don’t forget to tag your photographer so they capture every magical second! ✨

Why Do You Even Need Indonesian Songs at Your Wedding?

Let’s be real, guys. Indonesian songs have a magic of their own — the kind that gets every generation, from boomers to Gen Z, singing along. Plus, imagine how proud you’ll feel when a favourite track by a local artist rings out on your big day. It’s giving patriotic and romantic vibes at the same time!

Local music also carries an emotional weight that sits closer to our culture. Slow and mellow through to upbeat, Indonesian songs can cover all the feels you need across the whole reception.

So if you want the wedding vibes to feel more local and more heartfelt, these Indonesian tracks belong on your wedding playlist. Iconic love songs, slow pop, viral TikTok duets — all of it ready to get every guest singing along and feeling every bit of it!

Scroll straight down for the 30 romantic Indonesian-language songs that fit your wedding perfectly

1. Aku Dan Dirimu - Ari Lasso feat BCL Duet goals that have been making people emotional for years

2. Untukku - Chrisye A Chrisye classic that will always be timeless

3. Menikahimu - Kahitna Literally about getting married. Perfect.

4. Cantik - Kahitna A sweet appreciation song for your partner

5. Kasih Putih - Glenn Fredly RIP Glenn. The song is still a favourite.

6. Sempurna - Andra And The Backbone The love anthem that never misses at a wedding

7. Sedari Dulu - Tompi Smooth jazz vibes, seriously classy

8. Janji Suci - Yovie & Nuno Perfect for the moment you exchange vows

9. Cinta Pertama dan Terakhir - Sherina Childhood sweetheart vibes

10. Hari Bersamanya - Sheila on 7 An emotional rock ballad

11. Anugrah Terundah - Andmesh Viral on TikTok and perfect for a wedding

12. DIA - Anji Simple, but it lands

13. Karena Kucinta Kau - Bunga Citra Lestari BCL’s powerhouse vocals never disappoint

14. Kamu Yang Kutunggu - Rossa feat. Afgan A collaboration that melts you

15. Satu-Satunya - HIVI! Fresh, romantic indie pop

16. KISAH SEMPURNA - Mahalini A rising star with an amazing voice

17. Terlukis Indah - Rizky Febian & Ziva Magnolya Young talent that makes you proud

18. Pilihan Yang Terbaik - Ziva Magnolya A powerful solo performance

19. Menua Dalam Pelukan - Badai X Dudy Oris Viral and romantic — perfect combo

20. Ada - Lyodra feat. Afgan An Indonesian Idol winner with serious talent

21. Akhirnya Ku Menemukanmu - NaFF Finally-found-each-other energy

22. Semenjak Ada Dirimu - Andity Grateful-for-love vibes

23. Ada Cinta - Acha Septriasa & Irwansyah A sweet duet that’ll make you smile

24. Saat Bahagia - Ungu feat. Andien A celebration of happiness

25. Adu Rayu - Yovie Tulus Glenn Playful, fun wedding mood

26. Cinta Kan Membawamu Kembali - Reza For couples with a long-distance story

27. Bunga Abadi - Rio Clappy Eternal love symbolism

28. Primadona - Adikara Treating your partner like royalty

29. Niscaya - Bilal Indrajaya Promise and commitment vibes

30. Sampai Jadi Debu - Banda Neira feat. Gardika Gigih Till death do us part, Indonesian version

Pro Tips for Arranging Your Indonesian Wedding Playlist 🎧

Timing is Everything

  1. Ceremony entrance: go slow and emotional, something like "Kasih Putih" or "Untukku"
  2. First dance: go with the classics like "Sempurna" or "Menikahimu"
  3. Reception party: upbeat tracks like "Adu Rayu" and "Saat Bahagia"
  4. Closing: something meaningful, like "Sampai Jadi Debu"

Mix Old & New

Don’t lock yourself into one era. Blend the throwbacks every generation knows with contemporary hits that still feel fresh. Balance is key!

Consider Your Guests

If most of your guests are the older generation, lean into the classics. If they’re mostly millennials and Gen Z, feel free to include more recent hits.

Practice Pronunciation

Brief your wedding band on how to pronounce the artists’ names and the song titles properly. Small details matter!

Why Indonesian Wedding Songs Hit Different

  1. Cultural Connection: Indonesian lyrics speak directly to what marriage means in our culture.
  2. Language Familiarity: everyone understands the words, so the emotional impact lands harder.
  3. Singalong Factor: from the little kids to the grandparents, everyone can join in.
  4. Supporting Local: show some love to local musicians while celebrating your own love story.

Bonus Tip: Building a Wedding Playlist That’s Actually Balanced

  1. 40% Indonesian songs - the core emotional moments
  2. 30% international classics - universal appeal
  3. 20% current hits - keeps it fresh
  4. 10% personal favourites - your own story

Ready to build the ultimate Indonesian wedding playlist? Save this list and talk it through with your partner and your wedding organizer. And don’t forget to ask the band or the DJ to rehearse your picks in advance!

Above all, pick songs that mean something to your journey together. Music is the soundtrack of your love story! 🎵❤️

71000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000041.body_en:
Marriage isn’t only about love and whether the two of you click. It also runs into cultural values, beliefs, and myths handed down through generations. Two of them come up constantly — usually as a family debate: can you marry someone who shares your marga, the Batak clan name? And what if you’re 3, 6, or 9 years apart? People say that’s bad news. Is it?

If you’re stuck on this, let’s take them one at a time — light, but still logical and grounded. Not stiff, we promise, and still genuinely useful. Ready? Keep scrolling.

What Is a Same-Marga Marriage?

A same-marga marriage is a marriage between two people who carry the same marga, or family name. The idea matters most in Batak culture, where kinship runs deep and your marga is a central part of who you are socially.

1. Where the Ban Came From

In several Indonesian cultures, and in Batak adat in particular, marrying within your marga is taboo. Why? Because in Batak custom a marga works like one large extended family. Two people sharing a marga are treated as siblings — and marrying your own sibling is obviously off the table.

For example:

If your marga is “Siregar”, then everyone else named Siregar counts as family. So marrying another Siregar = a big no-no in Batak adat.

This isn’t universal, though. Outside Batak communities — among Javanese or Sundanese families, for instance — marga isn’t what decides whether a marriage can go ahead.

2. What About Religion?

In Islam, as long as the person isn’t mahram — someone you are forbidden to marry under sharia, such as a sibling, a mother, or an aunt — marrying within the same marga is perfectly fine. So where the blood relation is distant or absent altogether, you’re in the clear religiously.

3. Civil Law and Legality

Under Indonesian civil law there is no rule prohibiting marriage within the same marga. As long as both people meet the legal requirements to marry, it stands.

So the short version — a same-marga marriage is:

  1. Down to the adat of each ethnic group
  2. Religiously valid as long as the person isn’t mahram
  3. Legal under national law

A 3, 6, or 9-Year Age Gap: Myth or Fact?

Now for the one that makes plenty of couples think twice: an age gap of 3, 6, or 9 years. Supposedly it leaves a relationship less harmonious, or stops it lasting. Does it, though?

1. Where the “3-6-9” Myth Comes From

This one turns up widely in Chinese culture and in various local beliefs built around numerology — the study of numbers and the luck they carry. 3, 6 and 9 get treated as “perfect odd” numbers, which supposedly brings imbalance into a household.

To this day, though, there is no scientific evidence that actually backs it up.

2. The Fact: An Age Gap Doesn’t Decide Whether a Relationship Works

What actually matters:

  1. Communication
  2. Seeing things the same way
  3. Life goals pointing in the same direction
  4. Being able to respect each other

Real examples? Plenty of couples are 10+ years apart and going strong. Others are one year apart and divorced. So it comes back to how you two build the relationship, not the number.

3. What Psychology Says

In psychology, an age difference can shape how each person sees things and makes decisions. That isn’t a negative in itself. It can be complementary, as long as both people are aware of it and willing to learn from each other.

For instance: the older partner brings steadiness, the younger one brings energy and fresh momentum.

The Bottom Line: Love Isn’t Measured in Marga or Years

You can absolutely honour adat, but it’s worth looking at this through logic and faith as well. Don’t let a clan name or a number sink a healthy, loving relationship.

👉 So, same-marga marriage? Allowed, as long as the person isn’t mahram and you and your family are ready for the consequences (especially if you come from a group that holds its adat strictly).

👉 A 3, 6, or 9-year gap? There’s no evidence it brings bad luck. What counts isn’t the number — it’s the commitment.

71000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000041.title_en: Can You Marry Within the Same Marga? What About a 3, 6, or 9-Year Age Gap? Here Are the Facts

Looking for a wedding that’s low-fuss, more personal, but still memorable? If you (or your partner) aren’t comfortable in a crowd, a micro wedding might be exactly the right answer.

It isn’t only easy on the budget, either — the concept is having a real moment with millennials and Gen Z. And if you’re an introvert, i.e. much happier talking to the handful of people closest to you, micro wedding = dream wedding.

What Is a Micro Wedding?

A micro wedding is a wedding with a very short guest list — usually just 20 to 50 people. So you can picture it: the guests really are your inner circle, immediate family, close friends, and the people you genuinely love.

The trend took off during the COVID-19 pandemic, when everyone was forced into smaller parties. But here’s the thing: once the pandemic passed, micro weddings stuck around, because plenty of people had realised something — not everyone actually enjoys a huge party!

Why Are Micro Weddings Such a Good Fit for Introverts?

Introverts tend to:

  1. Feel uncomfortable in big crowds
  2. Need quiet space to recharge
  3. Prefer personal, meaningful interaction

So instead of shaking hands and making conversation with 300 guests, half of whom you may not even know, why not spend your special day with the people who are genuinely close to you? More quality, less quantity. Agreed?

The Upside of a Micro Wedding: Not Just for Introverts!

1. More Intimate & Personal

With a small guest list, the mood is warmer and more familiar. You and your partner get to genuinely spend time with everyone, rather than saying a quick hi and then disappearing into photos.

2. Easy on the Budget, Still Elegant

Fewer guests means you can put the budget into the things that matter more:

  1. Seriously premium catering 🍽️
  2. A small but gorgeous venue 💒
  3. The best photographer/videographer 📸
  4. Exclusive favours 🎁

3. Less Drama, Less Stress

No wrestling with a 300-person seating plan, no keeping distant relatives happy when you don’t even know who they are. Simpler all round, and drama-free.

What’s the Difference Between a Micro Wedding and an Intimate Wedding?

They’re both small and private, but a micro wedding and an intimate wedding aren’t the same thing. Here’s how they differ:

1. Guest Count

  1. Micro Wedding: just 20–50 guests. Usually only immediate family & your closest friends.
  2. Intimate Wedding: up to 100 guests. Colleagues, cousins and so on still make the list.

📝 Put simply: micro is very small; intimate is still small but more flexible.

2. How Long the Day Runs

  1. Micro: short, just the akad — the Islamic marriage ceremony — plus lunch or dinner together.
  2. Intimate: room for a whole run of events, from the reception to the cake cutting to an after-party.

📝 Put simply: micro wraps up quickly; intimate runs longer.

3. Cost

  1. Micro: cheaper. The money can go into things that matter, like photos and premium catering.
  2. Intimate: needs more, because there are more guests and a bigger venue.

📝 Put simply: micro suits an aesthetic wedding on a low budget.

4. Location

  1. Micro: your house, a garden, a small rooftop.
  2. Intimate: usually a large restaurant or a small hotel ballroom.

📝 Put simply: micro is more flexible and doesn’t need a big space.

5. Atmosphere

  1. Micro: very warm, very calm, very private. Right for you if you’re an introvert.
  2. Intimate: still close-knit, just a bit livelier.

📝 Put simply: a micro wedding is seriously calm. An intimate wedding is calm but still lively.

How to Pull Off a Micro Wedding

If the concept appeals, here are a few tips to keep your micro wedding running smoothly and still make it count:

1. Pick a Small but Beautiful Venue

You don’t need a big ballroom. Look for something outdoors — a villa, a garden cafe, a rooftop, or a tiny chapel with a warm, cosy feel.

2. Sweat the Details

Because there are so few guests, you can go all in on the small things:

  1. Personalised invitations
  2. Handmade favours
  3. Chairs & tables with unusual decor

3. Choose Vendors Who Get Your Vibe

Make sure your vendors — decor, photographer, MC — understand the micro wedding concept, so your day stays intimate instead of turning loud and crowded.

4. Build in Special Moments

Because the event is small, you have more room to create moments people remember:

  1. A toast with your guests
  2. A relaxed karaoke session
  3. Friends sharing stories

Micro Weddings: The Modern Way to Marry Without the Nerves

Wedding trends have shifted. Not everyone is chasing a huge party any more. What matters is that the sacred part and the happiness are things you can celebrate honestly, without having to perform for hundreds of guests.

A micro wedding isn’t just a trend. It’s a deliberate choice by people who value what a marriage actually means: joining together, not simply throwing a party.

So Who Does This Concept Suit?

  1. Introvert couples
  2. Couples on a limited budget who still want quality
  3. Couples who want a chill, natural, non-formal vibe
  4. Couples who’d rather not be the centre of attention in a crowd

In Closing: Small but Meaningful

Remember, a wedding isn’t about how big the party is, it’s about how deep the meaning runs. So if the micro wedding concept feels right for you, go for it. Don’t be afraid to do it differently.

And if you’ve already had a micro wedding, or you’re about to, share your experience too. It all helps the next couple figure it out ✨

In the run-up to the big day, our heads are usually full of decor, dress fittings, the reception playlist, and the prewedding shoot. But hold on. In the middle of all that wedding-prep euphoria, there’s one important thing that gets skipped constantly: your health and your partner’s.

Because getting married isn’t only about joining two hearts, it’s two bodies and two immune systems too. Which is exactly why the premarital check-up — a full health screening before you marry — matters so much. And it doesn’t stop there: to be genuinely ready for a day that’s going to be relentlessly busy, you can also treat yourself to something like a reflexology massage.

So let’s talk about why a premarital check-up and a bit of self-care matter so much when you’re about to get married. This article covers it properly, relaxed but useful, for every couple planning a wedding right now. 👰🤵

What Is a Premarital Check-Up?

A premarital check-up is a set of medical tests for couples about to marry. The point is to check your overall health, including the reproductive system and any potential genetic or infectious conditions.

Why does it matter? Because a health check before the wedding tells you whether there’s any risk of a condition being passed on to your future children, or of something affecting your life together down the line.

Picture it: you and your partner have worn yourselves out organising a wedding, and then something turns up that nobody caught early. Best avoided.

An Important Fact: Plenty of Couples Have No Idea They Aren’t Healthy

According to data from BKKBN (the National Population and Family Planning Board) in March 2022, out of every 100,000 couples about to marry:

  1. 17.8% had anaemia
  2. 18% had chronic energy deficiency

So BKKBN, together with the Ministry of Religious Affairs, now requires a premarital check-up for every couple planning to marry. It isn’t optional any more, it’s a standard step towards a healthier generation.

What Actually Gets Checked?

A premarital check-up usually covers a few core tests. Nothing to be scared or embarrassed about — it’s all done professionally, and it’s all for your benefit and your partner’s.

1. Blood Type & Rhesus Testing

This one matters because it tells you whether your rhesus (Rh) factors are compatible. Different rhesus factors can carry risk during pregnancy, especially from the first child onwards. The test also helps predict the risk of haemolytic disease in the baby, where the mother’s antibodies attack the baby’s blood cells. Frightening, right?

2. Blood Disorder Testing

This usually covers:

  1. Thalassaemia: a genetic condition where the body struggles to produce haemoglobin.
  2. Haemophilia: a blood clotting disorder.
  3. Sickle cell anaemia: red blood cells take on a sickle shape and can block blood vessels.

If you and your partner are both carriers of a particular blood disorder, your child could be at risk of developing it. Better to check now than regret it later.

3. Sexually Transmitted Infection (STI) Testing

Yes, this one is genuinely important! The screening usually covers the eight most common STIs:

  1. Chlamydia
  2. Gonorrhoea
  3. Syphilis
  4. Trichomonas
  5. Hepatitis B
  6. Herpes simplex
  7. HIV
  8. HPV (Human Papillomavirus)

Some of these can be cured; others can only be managed. The test also helps prevent transmission to your partner and to your future baby.

4. Genetic Testing

This checks whether you or your partner carry genes for conditions like haemophilia, thalassaemia, or other genetic disorders. It matters even more if there’s a family history of a particular condition.

What You and Your Partner Get Out of It

Here’s what a premarital check-up gives you:

  1. You each know exactly where your health stands
  2. Early detection of inherited or genetic conditions
  3. Help planning a healthy pregnancy
  4. Preventing transmission to your partner or your children
  5. It gets you and your partner being honest & open with each other

So a premarital check-up isn’t about hunting for problems. It’s about finding solutions and preparing properly for a future together.

And Don’t Forget the Self-Care Before the Big Day!

Stress can climb sharply in the run-up — vendors, guests, budget, family drama. To stay sane and glowing on the day itself, you need some “me time” too.

One favourite among couples about to marry:

✨ Reflexology Massage

Reflexology is a relaxation therapy focused on the nerve points in your feet and hands. What it does:

  1. Improves circulation
  2. Reduces stress and anxiety
  3. Helps you sleep better
  4. Boosts endorphins (the happy hormone!)

According to the journal Evidence-Based Complementary and Alternative Medicine (2014), reflexology has been shown to help with:

  1. Mild depression
  2. Sleep disorders
  3. Excessive anxiety (a.k.a. bridezilla symptoms!)

So if the wedding prep is starting to overwhelm you, go and book a reflexology session with a friend or your partner. You’ll be more relaxed, happier, and in much better shape on your special day.

Tips If You’re Booking a Premarital Check-Up

  1. Do it 3-6 months before the day, so there’s still time if further treatment turns out to be needed.
  2. Go together. This isn’t one person’s responsibility.
  3. Don’t be shy with the doctor. The more honest you are, the more accurate the diagnosis and the advice.
  4. Keep the results somewhere safe. They can be an important reference during pregnancy.

The Bottom Line: Marriage Needs More Than Love, It Needs Health Too!

Getting married doesn’t only join two hearts, it joins two states of health. With a premarital check-up, you and your partner can look after each other and be genuinely ready for the future together.

And don’t forget to look after your body and your head in the run-up. Reflexology and other treatments aren’t a luxury, they’re what keeps you healthy and happy.

So before you get busy picking napkin colours and invitations, make sure you and your partner have had that health check!

Getting married isn’t only about a grand reception, the dress you’ve dreamed about, or a honeymoon somewhere exotic. Marriage is a big decision that changes the direction of your life. And of course, the question that keeps coming up is: “So what age is actually ideal for getting married?”

So if you’re currently thinking about a future with your partner (or still working out who that partner is 😂), let’s talk it through together — the ideal age to get married, and not just in years, but mentally, emotionally and financially. Because being ready to marry doesn’t mean you’re simply worn down by everyone asking “When’s your turn?”

Marriage Isn’t a Race

Plenty of people still think of marriage as a competition: first past the post wins. But marriage isn’t a race. There’s no trophy for whoever gets there first. What actually matters is this: are you ready or not?

A mature marriage comes from being ready across a lot of areas, not simply from “I’m this age now” or “we’ve been dating a long time.” There’s plenty to think through — emotions, communication, money, and sexual readiness.

What Actually Makes You Ready to Marry

A few key factors shape whether someone is ready for marriage:

  1. Being old enough to have matured
  2. Emotional maturity
  3. Being able to communicate with your partner
  4. Sexual readiness
  5. Financial readiness

So it isn’t only about age, it’s about how ready you are, mentally and in terms of responsibility, to spend the long haul living alongside someone.

What the Experts Say: The Ideal Marrying Age According to BKKBN

If we’re going by official data, the head of the National Population and Family Planning Board (BKKBN), Dr Hasto Wardoyo, says that:

  1. The ideal age to marry for women is 21
  2. The ideal age to marry for men is 25

Why the difference? Because biologically and psychologically, men tend to mature more slowly than women. So those ages are considered enough time to prepare for the responsibility of running a household, or of becoming a mother.

The International View: 28 to 32 Is Ideal

Research from the National Survey of Family Growth (NSFG) in the United States puts the ideal marrying age somewhere between 28 and 32. By then, most people are more stable financially and emotionally, and have a more grown-up grasp of commitment and of living with a partner.

Fun fact: divorce rates in that age range are reported to be lower than for people who marry very young.

The Legal View: 19 at Minimum

Under Indonesian law — Law No. 16 of 2019, amending Law No. 1 of 1974 — it states that:

“Marriage is only permitted once the man and the woman have reached the age of 19.”

So if you and your partner haven’t hit that age, legally you can’t marry yet. One reason the law exists is the rising divorce rate among couples who marry young, mostly driven by small conflicts that drag on and on.

Why Do So Many Young Marriages End in Divorce?

Plenty of young couples marry out of love, or under pressure from the people around them, without enough in the tank to resolve household conflict. And problems in a marriage don’t stop at "in-law drama" or "an argument over curtain colours".

Common reasons for divorce among young couples:

  1. Not emotionally mature yet
  2. Struggling to communicate
  3. Taking offence easily
  4. Finances not yet stable
  5. Not enough understanding of sexuality and of each other’s roles

Learn From People Whose Marriages Work

One way to avoid a shock when you do get married is to learn from people already living a healthy marriage. It doesn’t have to be your parents — it could be a mentor, an older sibling, or a friend in a healthy, supportive relationship.

Why does this matter? Because from them you can learn how to:

  1. Respect your partner
  2. Handle conflict with a cool head
  3. Be a solid team instead of blaming each other

Financial and Sexual Readiness Are Non-Negotiable!

Marriage isn’t only about being able to pay the caterer and hire a WO. Once the reception is over your new life starts, and that needs consistent financial readiness. You don’t want to be a week in and already stuck on the electricity bill.

Beyond money, sexual readiness matters too. Plenty of couples walk into marriage without enough sex education, when it’s one of the key foundations of a healthy household.

So, When Is the Right Time to Marry?

The answer: when you’re genuinely ready.

You don’t have to wait until 30, but don’t rush into it out of FOMO (fear of missing out) or because of what people say, either. Measure your own readiness, not somebody else’s.

A checklist for gauging whether you’re ready:

  1. Legally old enough
  2. A steady income (or a realistic financial plan)
  3. Ready mentally & emotionally
  4. Able to communicate openly with your partner
  5. Some grounding in sex education and parenting
  6. A clear understanding of each other’s roles in the household

In Closing: Focus on Quality, Not Timing

Marriage is about the quality of the relationship and your readiness, not simply your age. There’s no fixed formula for an “ideal age,” there’s only ideal readiness. So if you’re wondering “Is it time to get married yet?”, try flipping the question into: “Am I ready to fight for one person for the rest of my life?”

If you are, go ahead! If you’re not, that’s fine too. Everyone’s path is different. What matters is that you’re happy and you’re ready.

A wedding isn't only about the lavish party, the dreamy decor, or that “you may kiss the bride” moment that melts every guest in the room. Behind all that euphoria sits a mountain of prep that demands you be in top physical and mental shape. So if you're counting down the days to your wedding, here's something worth knowing first: there's a whole list of things couples are advised to steer clear of.

These aren't just old wives' tales handed down by the grandparents either — think them through and most of them make real sense. Some are about health, some about safety, some about energy and stamina. So to keep you from crashing, or from anything going sideways on the day itself, here are the 5 big ones to avoid before you get married!

1. Don't Drive Alone, and Skip the Long Trips

Whether it's a weekend away or a low-key road trip, put it on hold for now. In Javanese belief and plenty of other local traditions, couples about to marry are advised not to travel far or drive themselves — bike or car, doesn't matter.

Why?

💡 It's genuinely logical. A long drive takes serious stamina and can leave you wiped out. Then there's the crash risk if you're on your own. And if something does go wrong, who's there to look after you?

Tips:

  1. If you do have to head out, try to bring someone with you.
  2. Cut out long-distance travel for at least 1 month before the day.
  3. Save the out-of-town or overseas honeymoon for after the reception!

2. Stop the All-Nighters, Please!

If you're the type who stays up late for work deadlines or a Korean drama binge, time to hit the brakes. In the run-up to a wedding you need your body in top form and your immune system strong. All-nighters will knock you flat.

Picture it: your wedding day, and you're running on empty — panda eyes, dull skin, mood swings, all from not sleeping. Big no.

Why the late nights really have to go:

  1. Your immune system drops → you get sick easily
  2. Skin breakouts & dullness
  3. You tire fast and get touchy
  4. Your emotions go all over the place (and that's a fast track to stress)

Tips:

  1. Sleep on a schedule, 7-8 hours a night minimum
  2. Go easy on the coffee and tea close to bedtime
  3. Build a wind-down routine (aromatherapy, gadgets off before bed)

3. No Mountain Climbing for Now!

If hiking or camping is your thing, this one might sting a bit. But in Kejawen belief and Javanese spiritual tradition, mountains are seen as places charged with powerful unseen energy. Couples about to marry are advised to hold off on climbing them.

Look at it practically and mountaineering is an extreme activity. Falls, sprains, hypothermia, even getting lost — all real risks. And you definitely don't want to be walking down the aisle in a cast or with a limp, right?

Tips:

  1. Turn the climb into a fun honeymoon plan with your partner instead
  2. Swap it for something gentler like yoga or a morning walk in the park

4. Don't Test-Drive New Skincare or Makeup!

You're probably itching to try that viral TikTok skincare product, or the pricey serum that supposedly makes you glow overnight. But... hold off! Coming up to the wedding, your skin needs stability, not experiments.

Trying new skincare or makeup can trigger breakouts, irritation, even an allergic reaction. And once that happens, trust us... even the best makeup artist will struggle to cover an angry red spot 😢

You also need to pay attention to what you're eating. Avoid:

  1. Food high in sugar and salt
  2. Anything too spicy or too acidic
  3. Fast food and processed food

Tips:

  1. Stick with the skincare that's already been working for you
  2. Eat well, drink enough water, and add plenty of fresh fruit
  3. Keep up some light exercise to help your body detox naturally

5. Don't Slip the Engagement Ring On and Off Carelessly

It sounds like superstition, but taking the engagement ring off too often before the wedding is said to bring “bad luck” or signal a relationship going cold. And even if you don't buy the mystical side of it, an engagement ring is a symbol of commitment with serious sentimental value.

The reality:

  1. Taking it off carelessly makes losing it much more likely
  2. Rings slip off, drop without you noticing, or you simply forget where you put it
  3. Lose it right before the day and you'll stress yourself out, when there's already plenty else on your plate

Tips:

  1. If you do have to take it off (in the shower, or to sleep), keep it somewhere specific
  2. Make a habit of taking it off and storing it in the same spot so you don't forget
  3. For extra safety, get a cute ring-holder necklace so it stays on you

Bonus: Don't Skip Your Me Time and Downtime

In among all the rules and checklists you have to work through, make time to switch off and be on your own. Look after your sanity. Getting married is beautiful, but the prep will burn you out if you never get a chance to recharge.

Me-time ideas for couples about to marry:

  1. A reflexology massage or a spa day
  2. Journaling or a bit of light meditation
  3. Quality time with your closest friends
  4. A short staycation just to unwind
  5. A digital detox (put the phone down for a while!)

To Wrap Up: Physical and Mental Prep Is the Whole Game

In the run-up to your wedding you don't only need an invitation checklist or a vendor list — you need solid physical, mental and spiritual preparation. The things above might sound old-fashioned, but look at them logically and health-wise and every one has a strong reason behind it.

So, to all the brides-to-be and grooms-to-be out there, take good care of yourself. Because you're the headline act on that stage of love ❤️

Don't forget to keep up to date with wedding trends and the latest news by following 7Magic Organizer on Instagram so nothing passes you by!

If you're hunting for a wedding venue in Singapore that feels luxurious, classy and genuinely unforgettable, read this one all the way to the end. We've curated the 10 five-star hotels couples love most for weddings, based on real reviews from couples and wedding planners. Not only because the facilities are top tier, but because the atmosphere makes your big moment feel like a scene out of a romantic film!

So let's go through them one by one. One of them might click straight away 💍✨

1. Grand Hyatt Singapore – Stylish, Central and Endlessly Flexible

Location: Orchard Road

Review: “The venue is huge and you can customise it to your theme. The events team is so helpful!”

If you like a wedding concept that's modern and pared-back but still glamorous, Grand Hyatt should be top of the list. Their ballroom has an elegant design with adjustable lighting. And the location is so central that local and international guests alike can get there easily.

Standout features:

  1. Complete wedding packages
  2. Ballroom options from intimate to large
  3. An in-house kitchen with an international menu & halal certification

2. The Fullerton Hotel – A Wedding Against a Classic Heritage Backdrop

Location: Fullerton Square

Review: “I love the heritage vibe. Elegant but still warm and welcoming.”

If you and your partner lean classic and love a bit of history, the Fullerton is your answer. This colonial-style building isn't only Instagrammable, it's genuinely iconic in Singapore. A wedding here feels like a Southeast Asian royal wedding.

Standout features:

  1. Views over Marina Bay & the Singapore River
  2. A classic European-style ballroom
  3. An in-house wedding planning team

3. The St. Regis Singapore – An Ultra-Exclusive Wedding Fit for Aristocracy

Location: Tanglin Road

Review: “From the interiors to the service, everything is high-class. Like getting married in a castle!”

St. Regis has a reputation as the luxury hotel for premium events. Baroque interiors and a collection of expensive art lift the whole atmosphere. Its ballroom is known as one of the most beautiful in Singapore.

Standout features:

  1. Caroline’s Mansion as a private venue
  2. A custom menu by a Michelin-starred chef
  3. The iconic champagne sabrage ceremony

4. Mandarin Oriental – A Marina Bay View That Leaves You Speechless

Location: Raffles Avenue

Review: “The ballroom looks straight out at Marina Bay. Sunset here is pure magic.”

Want to get married while taking in Singapore's most iconic view? Mandarin Oriental has ballrooms and function rooms looking directly over Marina Bay. Perfect for a golden-hour wedding that's romantic and epic in equal measure.

Standout features:

  1. All-in wedding packages
  2. Halal and vegetarian menu options
  3. Elegant decor you can customise

5. JW Marriott Hotel Singapore South Beach – Chic & Futuristic

Location: Beach Road

Review: “The design is brilliant, perfect for a young couple who want something different.”

This hotel suits you if you're drawn to a modern, edgy feel. Futuristic interiors and artful lighting make your wedding stand apart. The ballroom comes with an LED wall and a serious audio system!

Standout features:

  1. An LED runway for the wedding entrance
  2. Indoor & outdoor rooftop venues
  3. A team of professional wedding specialists

6. Shangri-La Singapore – A Garden Wedding in the Middle of the City

Location: Orange Grove Road

Review: “I couldn't believe you could get a garden wedding this peaceful in the middle of the city.”

Shangri-La is the one if you want a natural wedding theme that still reads glamorous. They have a big garden venue that can be turned into a full fairytale wedding setting!

Standout features:

  1. An outdoor wedding garden
  2. Multiple ballroom options
  3. A popular Chinese banquet menu

7. Capella Singapore – A Private Wedding on Sentosa Island

Location: Sentosa

Review: “Spot on for an intimate wedding. It feels like a private island wedding!”

Capella has a genuinely secluded, exclusive feel. Ideal if you want private, intimate and luxury in one package. Plus the resort is wrapped in lush tropical greenery.

Standout features:

  1. An outdoor lawn with an ocean view
  2. A luxury villa for the bridal suite
  3. Personal service from their wedding team

8. Raffles Hotel Singapore – Classic & Timeless Elegance

Location: Beach Road

Review: “The venue is classic and seriously classy. Perfect for a wedding with an old-money feel.”

If you love a classic 1920s wedding mood, Raffles is the obvious pick. The hotel is steeped in history and the colonial architecture is stunning.

Standout features:

  1. The Tiffin Room & Jubilee Ballroom
  2. All-inclusive wedding packages
  3. A hugely experienced F&B team

9. Andaz Singapore – A Stylish, Instagram-Ready Wedding

Location: Bugis

Review: “The venue is artsy and chic. Great for a modern wedding party.”

This hotel has no shortage of good-looking corners for the photo session. A modern ballroom with natural light, a rooftop bar and food stations give it a thoroughly current feel.

Standout features:

  1. A rooftop wedding view
  2. Open-kitchen buffet style
  3. Artsy & photogenic interior design

10. The Ritz-Carlton, Millenia Singapore – Wedding of the Year Vibes

Location: Marina Bay

Review: “Everyone said our wedding looked like a red carpet event. Thank you Ritz!”

The Ritz-Carlton never misses on luxury. The ballroom is vast and can be reworked to fit any theme. Ideal for a big wedding with VVIP guests.

Standout features:

  1. A grand ballroom with a 7-metre LED wall
  2. Floral ceiling decoration
  3. A bridal suite with a Marina Bay view

How to Choose Your Wedding Hotel in Singapore

Still torn on which hotel to go with? Weigh up a few things:

  1. Wedding theme: classic, modern, or outdoor?
  2. Guest numbers: make sure the ballroom actually fits everyone on the list.
  3. Facilities: is there a bridal suite? A halal menu? A decent sound system?
  4. Budget: don't forget to keep it in line with what you and your partner can spend!

To Wrap Up: Make Your Once-in-a-Lifetime Moment Count ✨

Getting married in a five-star hotel in Singapore isn't only about the luxury — it's about the experience. From the best service going to a venue that stops people in their tracks, it's all built to make your day truly unforgettable.
